domain_label: Plated Jewelry — Launch Test-and-Iterate Protocol, Keep/Cut/Expand Rule & SKU-Bloat Discipline
purpose: A method for running the launched 6-SKU plated-jewelry set as a controlled test — defining the sell-through, return/quality and contribution-margin metrics, fixing the honest measurement window and sample sufficiency before any verdict, applying a keep/cut/expand decision rule, then setting a refresh cadence that expands winners and prunes losers without drifting into SKU bloat — while never inventing a benchmark sell-through, return rate or margin threshold that only the store's own data can supply.
assumptions: the launch set of 6 SKUs and their production/economics constraints are inherited as input from kb2_launch_set_of_six and the economics specialist; this KB does not re-derive them

sell-through rate = units sold / units received over a defined window, and contribution margin = net price minus variable cost per unit, are standard [FACT-retail/managerial-accounting] definitions used here, not invented metrics

no benchmark 'good' sell-through %, return %, or margin threshold is asserted as a measured industry fact; keep/cut thresholds are [METHOD]/[ESTIMATE] the owner calibrates against the store's own baseline and cost stack

the measurement window and sample-sufficiency reasoning rest on real small-sample-noise / statistical-power facts [FACT-statistics]; the specific unit counts named are [ESTIMATE] planning bands, not claims about this store

plated-jewelry return drivers (ring sizing, plating wear/tarnish, nickel skin reaction per EN1811 0.5 ug/cm2/week) are real domain facts [FACT]; their realised rates for this store are [UNKNOWN] until measured
every non-fact is tagged [ESTIMATE] (method+confidence), [METHOD] (how to measure it) or [UNKNOWN]; real retail/statistics/materials facts are tagged [FACT] with basis
exclusions: constructing the initial launch set of 6 (kb2_launch_set_of_six owns that; this KB starts after launch)
synthesizing and ranking the pre-launch demand signals (kb1_signal_synthesis_ranking owns the market+poll+store-data blend)
the full unit-economics / pricing / CAC-LTV model (the economics specialist owns COGS, price and viability; this KB consumes contribution margin as an input metric)
the poll instrument design and paid-reach mechanics (the poll specialist owns those; this KB only feeds learnings back to them)
asserting a specific numeric benchmark for sell-through, return rate or margin as a measured market fact, or fabricating this store's realised rates before they are observed

competency_questions.question: What are the core post-launch metrics for a plated-jewelry SKU test and how is each defined?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: METRIC_DEFINITIONS names sell-through, return/quality rate and contribution margin per SKU with their standard [FACT] formulas, and LAUNCH_BASELINE_INPUT establishes the 6-SKU launch set and its baseline as the accepted test input

competency_questions.question: How long / how much volume must accumulate before a keep-or-cut verdict is honest rather than noise?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MEASUREMENT_WINDOW states the window as a [METHOD] with a statistical/seasonal basis and SAMPLE_SUFFICIENCY states why a handful of orders is small-sample noise, both tagged so no early verdict is treated as signal

competency_questions.question: How is per-SKU sell-through computed and read against the store's own baseline rather than an invented benchmark?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SELL_THROUGH_RATE states units-sold/units-received over the window as [FACT-def] and flags any 'good' threshold as [METHOD] calibrated to the store, never a fabricated industry number

competency_questions.question: How is the return/quality-complaint rate measured and attributed to plated-jewelry-specific causes?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RETURN_QUALITY_RATE states the return-rate formula and attributes returns to sizing, plating wear/tarnish and nickel reaction ([FACT] drivers) with realised rates flagged [UNKNOWN] until measured

competency_questions.question: How does contribution margin per SKU enter the keep/cut decision and where does it come from?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONTRIBUTION_MARGIN_SKU states margin = net price minus variable cost per unit [FACT], inherited from the economics specialist, and net of returns/markdowns so a high-return SKU is not judged on gross margin alone

competency_questions.question: How are the three metrics combined into one comparable per-SKU score without letting one metric mask another?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMPOSITE_SCORE defines a transparent weighted blend of sell-through, margin and return rate as a [METHOD] and states the weights are owner-set priors re-calibrated over cycles, not fabricated constants

competency_questions.question: What is the keep/cut/expand decision rule and how does it handle winners, losers and the ambiguous middle?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: KEEP_CUT_EXPAND_RULE states the decision-matrix [METHOD] gated on sample sufficiency, WINNER_EXPANSION and LOSER_CUT_DISCONTINUE state the expand/discontinue actions, and AMBIGUOUS_HOLD_TWEAK states the hold-and-tweak path for under-powered or confounded SKUs

competency_questions.question: What confounds a per-SKU signal, and how are marketing, price changes and seasonality separated from true product performance?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ATTRIBUTION_CONFOUNDS names ad-spend/price/merchandising confounds and SEASONALITY_ADJUST names the gift-cycle seasonality (Q4/Valentine's/Mother's Day [FACT]) that distorts a raw sell-through read across the window

competency_questions.question: How often should new SKUs be introduced and old ones dropped — the refresh cadence?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REFRESH_CADENCE states a drop-in/drop-out cadence as a [METHOD] tied to the measurement window and MOQ reorder cycle, not an arbitrary calendar, so newness is added without out-running the ability to measure it

competency_questions.question: How is SKU bloat avoided as winners are expanded and the catalog grows?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SKU_BLOAT_AVOIDANCE states one-in-one-out / long-tail carrying-cost discipline as a [METHOD] and CANNIBALIZATION_CHECK states that a new variant must add incremental demand, not just steal an existing winner's sales

competency_questions.question: How do plating-run MOQ and working capital constrain how fast a SKU can be expanded or cut?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INVENTORY_MOQ_CONSTRAINT states that plating-batch MOQ and the cash tied in a losing SKU's stock set a floor on cut/expand speed, so a cut decision must plan markdown/liquidation of committed inventory

competency_questions.question: How is the protocol's honesty discipline enforced and what is handed to the next launch cycle and back to the demand read?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HONESTY_LEDGER separates [FACT] metric definitions from [METHOD]/[ESTIMATE] thresholds and [UNKNOWN] realised rates, FEEDBACK_TO_DEMAND routes learnings back to the poll/market read, and ITERATION_HANDOFF delivers the cut/keep/expand set plus the refresh calendar and guardrails

glossary.definition: The share of received inventory sold over a defined window: units sold / units received (or / (units received + opening stock)) [FACT-retail metric]. The primary demand signal per SKU, but only meaningful once enough units have been received and enough time/volume has passed to escape small-sample noise; a 'good' sell-through band is [METHOD] calibrated to this store's own baseline, never a fabricated industry constant.

Returns (and quality complaints/warranty claims) as a share of units sold over the window. For plated jewelry the load-bearing drivers are ring-size mismatch, plating wear/tarnish, and nickel-release skin reaction (EN1811 limit 0.5 ug/cm2/week for prolonged contact) [FACT-drivers]; the realised per-SKU rate for this store is [UNKNOWN] until measured. A high return rate can quietly erase a SKU's apparent margin.

Net selling price minus variable cost per unit (COGS + variable selling/fulfilment + return/markdown allowance) [FACT-managerial accounting], inherited from the economics specialist. The keep/cut rule uses contribution net of returns and markdowns, so a SKU that sells fast but returns heavily or discounts deeply is not flattered by its gross margin.

The minimum elapsed time and accumulated volume before a keep/cut/expand verdict is honest rather than noise [METHOD with statistical+seasonal basis]. Set by two forces: statistical power (enough units for the sell-through/return estimate to be stable [FACT-small-sample noise]) and seasonality (span or adjust for the gift cycle so a Valentine's spike or a January lull is not mistaken for product signal).

Whether a SKU has accumulated enough sales for its measured rates to be trustworthy [FACT-statistical power]. A handful of orders produces a sell-through/return estimate with a wide confidence interval; ranking SKUs on tiny samples over-fits to noise. Under-powered SKUs are routed to hold-and-tweak, not cut, until the window and volume gates are met.

The decision matrix [METHOD] that maps a SKU's composite performance, gated on sample sufficiency, to one of three actions: KEEP (steady performer, reorder at depth), EXPAND (proven winner, add variants/colours/depth), or CUT (structural loser, discontinue and liquidate). The ambiguous middle (weak or confounded signal) is held and tweaked, not force-decided.

The uncontrolled growth of the catalog into a long tail of low-velocity SKUs, each carrying inventory cash, plating-run MOQ, photography and cognitive-load costs while contributing little demand [FACT-operations]. The antidote is assortment discipline: one-in-one-out, a hard cut rule for persistent losers, and a cannibalization check so new variants add incremental demand.

The rhythm of introducing new candidate SKUs and dropping discontinued ones [METHOD]. Tied to the measurement window (do not launch faster than you can measure) and the plating-batch MOQ / reorder cycle (do not commit newness the cash cycle cannot fund), so the catalog stays fresh without out-running the test protocol or the working capital.

The degree to which a new or expanded variant steals sales from an existing SKU rather than adding incremental demand [METHOD to estimate]. A winner-expansion that only redistributes the same buyers inflates SKU count and cost without growing revenue; the check compares total category velocity before/after against the new SKU's own sales.

Any factor other than intrinsic product appeal that moves a SKU's measured sell-through — a burst of ad spend, a price change, a homepage feature, a seasonal gift peak, or an influencer post [FACT-causal-inference caution]. Confounds must be flagged before a cut/expand verdict, because a SKU can look like a winner purely because it was promoted.

nodes.definition: Accept the launched set of 6 SKUs (from kb2_launch_set_of_six) plus the store's existing baseline as the input this protocol tests, without re-deriving either. Record for each SKU: units received/on hand, launch date, price, category, and the pre-launch expectation (the ranked signal from kb1) so measured performance can be read against a prior, not a vacuum. Establish that launch is the START of a controlled test, not the end of the decision: the six are hypotheses to be measured, kept, cut or expanded, and 'mindful of the old stuff' means the existing store's velocity and returns baseline is carried as the comparison line. All pre-launch expectations are [ESTIMATE] priors; the realised data is [UNKNOWN] until the window closes.

included: the 6 launched SKUs and the store baseline as accepted test input
per-SKU units, price, category, launch date and the kb1 prior expectation
framing launch as the start of a measured test

pros.claim: Carrying the pre-launch prior alongside the launch set lets measured performance be read as beat/miss versus expectation, not as a raw number in a vacuum
pros.example: a SKU ranked #1 by kb1 that sells slowly is a more informative miss than an unranked SKU selling slowly

cons.claim: Anchoring on the pre-launch prior risks confirmation bias, keeping a favoured SKU alive past its measured performance
cons.example: a hero SKU the owner championed may be given too long before a cut

failure_modes: treating launch as the final decision rather than the start of a measured test
discarding the existing store baseline so new-SKU performance has no comparison line
acceptance_tests: the 6 launched SKUs, their per-SKU inputs and the store baseline are stated as accepted test input with the kb1 prior expectation carried per SKU
revisit_triggers: kb2 revises the launch set or a SKU is swapped pre-launch
the store baseline velocity/returns line is updated
a launch date or received-quantity changes

base.update_signal: the launch set, baseline or a per-SKU launch input changes

nodes.definition: Define the three load-bearing metrics the whole protocol runs on, with their standard formulas, so every downstream verdict rests on one agreed definition. (1) Sell-through rate = units sold / units received over the window [FACT-retail metric]. (2) Return/quality-complaint rate = returns / units sold over the window [FACT-def], attributed to plated-jewelry causes downstream. (3) Contribution margin per SKU = net price minus variable cost per unit, net of returns and markdowns [FACT-managerial accounting], inherited from the economics specialist. State that these definitions are fixed facts, while any threshold applied to them ('good' sell-through, 'acceptable' return, 'minimum' margin) is a [METHOD]/[ESTIMATE] the owner calibrates to the store, never a fabricated benchmark.

included: sell-through, return/quality and contribution-margin definitions and formulas [FACT]
the fact/threshold split (definitions are fact, thresholds are calibrated method)
excluded: the measurement window that bounds each metric (MEASUREMENT_WINDOW)
the per-metric measurement detail (the metric nodes)

pros.claim: Fixing one agreed definition per metric prevents downstream disputes about what a number means and keeps the fact/threshold line clean
pros.example: defining sell-through as units-sold/units-received stops a later reorder decision from silently switching to a revenue-based measure

cons.claim: Three clean metrics can under-describe a SKU whose value is strategic (category coverage, stacking, photography) rather than direct velocity
cons.example: an anchor SKU that anchors a collection but sells modestly is under-served by a pure sell-through view

failure_modes: applying an invented industry benchmark to a metric as if it were a measured fact
conflating gross margin with contribution net of returns and markdowns
acceptance_tests: sell-through, return/quality and contribution-margin definitions are stated with [FACT] formulas and the fact-vs-calibrated-threshold split is made explicit
revisit_triggers: the economics specialist revises the contribution-margin definition or cost inputs
a new metric (e.g. attach rate) is added to the protocol
the store's data system changes how units-sold or returns are recorded

base.update_signal: a metric definition or cost input is revised

nodes.definition: Fix the measurement window: the minimum elapsed time AND accumulated volume before a keep/cut/expand verdict is honest rather than noise [METHOD with a real statistical+seasonal basis]. Two forces set it. (1) Statistical power: a sell-through or return estimate is unstable until enough units have sold; deciding on a few orders over-reads noise [FACT-small-sample]. (2) Seasonality: jewelry demand is heavily gift-cyclical (Q4 holiday, Valentine's, Mother's Day, graduation) [FACT-general retail], so a window that straddles a spike or a lull must span or adjust for it. The concrete window (e.g. a planning band of ~4-8 weeks OR a per-SKU unit threshold, whichever comes later) is an [ESTIMATE] the owner tunes to traffic; the principle that you do not judge before the window closes is the fixed [METHOD]. Cutting a SKU inside its window is the single most common test-and-iterate error.

included: time-and-volume window as a [METHOD]
the statistical-power and seasonality bases
the ~4-8 week / unit-threshold band as an [ESTIMATE] planning anchor

pros.claim: Fixing a window before launch stops premature culls driven by a slow first week that says nothing
pros.example: a SKU written off after 5 sales in week 1 might be a steady seller once its window and traffic accumulate

cons.claim: A long window ties up cash in a possibly-dead SKU and slows the iteration loop, trading speed for confidence
cons.example: waiting 8 weeks on a clear structural loser wastes two months of shelf and cash

failure_modes: declaring a verdict inside the window on a slow or fast first few days
setting a calendar-only window that ignores whether enough units actually sold
acceptance_tests: the window is stated as a time-AND-volume [METHOD] with the statistical-power and seasonality bases and the ~4-8 week / unit-threshold band flagged [ESTIMATE]
revisit_triggers: site traffic changes materially, moving how fast the unit threshold is hit
the launch straddles a known seasonal spike or lull
a live sell-through curve shows the estimate stabilising earlier or later than assumed

base.update_signal: traffic, seasonality or the observed sell-through curve changes the window

nodes.definition: State the per-SKU sample-sufficiency gate that sits on top of the window: even after the calendar window passes, a low-traffic SKU may not have accumulated enough sales for its measured rates to be trustworthy [FACT-statistical power]. A sell-through or return-rate estimate from a handful of orders has a wide confidence interval, so ranking SKUs on tiny samples over-fits to noise and can cut a good SKU or expand a lucky one. The gate: a SKU with too few units sold (a threshold the owner sets, an [ESTIMATE] tied to acceptable estimate error) is NOT eligible for a cut/expand verdict — it is routed to hold-and-tweak (raise its exposure, fix its listing) to gather more data. This prevents the classic error of treating a 2-of-10 sell-through as a reliable signal.

included: per-SKU minimum-sales gate as a power/noise control
routing under-powered SKUs to hold-and-tweak not cut
the unit threshold as an owner-set [ESTIMATE]

pros.claim: Gating verdicts on sample size stops noise-driven culls and lucky-streak expansions on thinly-sold SKUs
pros.example: a SKU at 3 sales is held for more exposure rather than cut, avoiding a noise-based discontinue

cons.claim: A high sufficiency bar can strand a genuinely dead low-traffic SKU in perpetual hold, never accumulating enough to cut cleanly
cons.example: a SKU that gets almost no impressions may never reach the threshold, needing a traffic-side decision instead

failure_modes: ranking or cutting SKUs on single-digit sample sizes as if the rates were stable
letting an under-powered SKU sit in hold forever without a traffic or exposure fix
acceptance_tests: the minimum-sales sufficiency gate, its statistical-power basis, and the route-to-hold-not-cut rule are stated with the unit threshold flagged [ESTIMATE]
revisit_triggers: the owner tightens or loosens the acceptable estimate-error tolerance
a SKU sits under-powered past a second window
traffic allocation changes which SKUs accumulate samples

base.update_signal: the sufficiency threshold or a SKU's accumulated sample changes

nodes.definition: Measure per-SKU sell-through over the window: units sold / units received [FACT-def], reported alongside velocity (units/week) so a SKU with little stock is not flattered by a high percentage. This is the primary demand signal — it answers 'did buyers actually want this piece' more directly than clicks or poll votes (which kb1 already discounted for self-selection bias). Critical honesty rule: there is NO fabricated 'good' sell-through benchmark; the reference line is this store's own baseline velocity for comparable pieces (the 'old stuff' from LAUNCH_BASELINE_INPUT) plus the pre-launch expectation. A 'winner' band and a 'loser' band are [METHOD] cut points the owner sets against that baseline and the reorder economics, re-calibrated each cycle — never an industry number asserted as fact.

included: sell-through and velocity per SKU over the window
baseline+prior as the reference line, not an invented benchmark
winner/loser bands as owner-calibrated [METHOD] cut points
excluded: the composite blend with margin and returns (COMPOSITE_SCORE)
the confounds that distort the raw read (ATTRIBUTION_CONFOUNDS)

pros.claim: Reporting sell-through with velocity and against the store's own baseline gives an honest demand read without inventing a benchmark
pros.example: a 40% sell-through on 50 units means more than 80% on 5 units, and both are judged against the store's comparable-piece baseline

cons.claim: Raw sell-through conflates product appeal with exposure and price, so it is misleading until confounds are removed
cons.example: a homepage-featured SKU out-sells an equally good buried SKU purely on placement

failure_modes: quoting a percentage without the underlying unit count or velocity
importing a fabricated 'average sell-through' as the benchmark instead of the store baseline
acceptance_tests: per-SKU sell-through and velocity over the window are stated with the store-baseline reference and the winner/loser bands flagged as owner-calibrated [METHOD], not an invented benchmark
revisit_triggers: the store baseline velocity is re-measured
received quantities change the denominator materially
a confound (feature, promo, price) is found to have driven the read

base.update_signal: the sell-through read, baseline, or a confound changes

nodes.definition: Measure per-SKU returns and quality complaints over the window: returns / units sold [FACT-def], with reason codes attributed to plated-jewelry-specific causes, because a plated piece can fail in ways an apparel SKU cannot. The load-bearing drivers [FACT]: ring-size mismatch (a sizing-driven return the form specialist's kb3 flags), plating wear / tarnish (thin or poorly-adhered rhodium/gold plating showing base metal), and nickel-release skin reaction (EN1811 limit 0.5 ug/cm2/week for prolonged contact). A high return or complaint rate is a hidden margin killer and a brand-trust risk: a SKU that sells well but returns heavily or draws tarnish complaints is a cut/fix candidate, not a keep. The realised per-SKU rate is [UNKNOWN] until measured; reason-code capture at return is the [METHOD] that makes it attributable rather than a lump number.

included: return/complaint rate per SKU with plated-jewelry reason codes
sizing, plating-wear/tarnish and nickel-reaction as [FACT] drivers
reason-code capture as the attribution [METHOD]

pros.claim: Capturing reason codes turns a lump return rate into an actionable diagnosis distinguishing a fixable sizing issue from a structural plating-quality failure
pros.example: a spike coded to tarnish points at plating thickness (a materials fix), while one coded to sizing points at the size chart (a listing fix)

cons.claim: Return reasons are self-reported and often mis-coded or blank, so the attribution carries measurement error
cons.example: a buyer returning for 'changed my mind' may actually have hit a tarnish or fit problem

failure_modes: judging a SKU on sell-through alone while ignoring a return rate that erases its margin
recording returns as a lump with no reason code, losing the fixable-vs-structural distinction
acceptance_tests: per-SKU return/complaint rate with plated-jewelry reason codes (sizing, plating wear/tarnish, nickel reaction) is stated with realised rates flagged [UNKNOWN] until measured
revisit_triggers: a return-reason spike appears on a specific SKU
a plating-quality or nickel-safety issue is reported
the sizing/fit chart is revised and re-tested

base.update_signal: a return-reason spike or a plating/nickel/sizing issue changes the rate

nodes.definition: Bring in per-SKU contribution margin as the third metric: net selling price minus variable cost per unit (COGS from the economics specialist + variable fulfilment + a return/markdown allowance) [FACT-managerial accounting]. This KB does not re-derive COGS; it consumes contribution as an input and insists it be read NET of returns and markdowns, so a SKU that sells fast but returns heavily or discounts deeply is not judged on its gross margin. A structural loser on margin (contribution near or below zero after returns) is a cut candidate even if it sells, because velocity at negative contribution loses money faster. Margin per SKU also feeds the expand decision: a winner with strong contribution is a better expansion bet than a winner with thin margin, since expansion commits more inventory cash.

included: contribution margin per SKU net of returns/markdowns as an inherited input
negative-contribution-despite-velocity as a cut signal
margin as an expansion-quality gate
excluded: deriving COGS, price or CAC (the economics specialist)

pros.claim: Reading margin net of returns and markdowns stops a high-velocity, high-return or heavily-discounted SKU from masquerading as a winner
pros.example: a fast SKU at 30% return and a 20% markdown may contribute less than a slower full-price SKU

cons.claim: Contribution per SKU inherits the economics specialist's cost uncertainty, so a thin-margin verdict is only as firm as the COGS input
cons.example: an [UNKNOWN] plating-consumption cost swings whether a SKU is marginally positive or negative

failure_modes: keeping a high-velocity SKU that contributes near zero after returns and markdowns
using gross margin instead of contribution net of returns in the cut/keep call
acceptance_tests: contribution margin per SKU net of returns/markdowns is stated as an inherited [FACT-defined] input, with negative-contribution-despite-velocity flagged as a cut signal
revisit_triggers: the economics specialist updates COGS or price for a SKU
a SKU's markdown or return allowance changes its contribution sign
input cost (plating, base metal, findings) moves materially

base.update_signal: a COGS, price, markdown or return-allowance input changes contribution

nodes.definition: Establish that a raw sell-through number is not a clean product signal until confounds are removed [FACT-causal-inference caution]. The confounds that move a plated-jewelry SKU's measured performance independent of its intrinsic appeal: a burst of paid ad spend pointed at it, a price change or promo, a homepage/collection feature, an influencer or UGC post, and email/SMS pushes. A SKU can look like a winner purely because it was promoted, and a good SKU can look like a loser because it was buried. Before any cut/expand verdict, flag each SKU's exposure and price history over the window; where a confound dominates, the SKU is routed to hold-and-tweak (normalise exposure, then re-measure) rather than decided. This is what stops the protocol from expanding a SKU that only sold because of a one-off ad push.

included: ad-spend, price, feature, influencer and email confounds
flag-exposure-and-price-history before verdict
route confounded SKUs to hold-and-tweak

pros.claim: Flagging confounds before a verdict prevents expanding a promotion-driven false winner or cutting a buried false loser
pros.example: a SKU that only sold during a paid boost is held and re-measured at normal exposure before any expansion

cons.claim: Full confound control needs disciplined tracking of exposure/price the owner may not have, so attribution stays partial
cons.example: without per-SKU impression data, feature effects can only be roughly flagged, not quantified

failure_modes: reading a promo-driven spike as intrinsic product appeal and expanding on it
cutting a good SKU that merely lacked exposure during the window
acceptance_tests: the ad/price/feature/influencer/email confounds and the flag-before-verdict + route-to-hold rule are stated so a confounded SKU is not force-decided
revisit_triggers: a SKU's exposure or price changed materially during the window
per-SKU impression/ad tracking becomes available
an influencer or UGC post drives a spike

base.update_signal: a SKU's exposure/price history or tracking availability changes

nodes.definition: Handle the seasonal confound specifically, because jewelry is one of the most gift-cyclical categories: demand concentrates around Q4 holiday, Valentine's Day, Mother's Day, graduations and wedding season [FACT-general retail], and a young-women audience (18-25) adds its own occasion pattern. A measurement window that straddles a spike over-reads every SKU as a winner; one in a lull under-reads them. The adjustment [METHOD]: either span the window across a comparable non-peak period, or normalise a SKU's window sell-through against the store's overall traffic/sales index for the same days, so a SKU is judged on its share of demand, not the absolute level a holiday inflated. Never launch-test a SKU only during a peak and expand on the peak number — its steady-state velocity is what must clear the keep/cut bar.

included: the jewelry gift-cycle peaks and lulls [FACT]
span-or-normalise-against-traffic-index adjustment [METHOD]
the do-not-expand-on-a-peak-number rule

pros.claim: Normalising against the traffic index lets a SKU be judged on its share of demand rather than a holiday-inflated absolute
pros.example: a SKU that sold well only because it launched in December is judged on its share of December traffic, not the raw December count

cons.claim: Seasonal normalisation needs enough history to know the store's own pattern, which a new store lacks
cons.example: a first-year store has no prior December to compare this December against

failure_modes: expanding a SKU on a peak-season number that will not hold at steady state
cutting a SKU tested only in a lull that would sell in season
acceptance_tests: the gift-cycle peaks, the span-or-normalise-against-traffic adjustment [METHOD], and the do-not-expand-on-a-peak rule are stated
revisit_triggers: the test window overlaps a known seasonal peak or lull
a full seasonal cycle of store history becomes available
the audience's occasion pattern shifts

base.update_signal: the window's seasonal position or available store history changes

nodes.definition: Combine the three metrics into one comparable per-SKU score so no single metric masks another [METHOD]. A transparent weighted blend of (normalised) sell-through, contribution margin and the inverse of return rate — e.g. score = w1*sell_through + w2*margin - w3*return_rate — with weights that are explicit, owner-set priors reflecting the business's current goal (cash generation favours margin; share growth favours sell-through), re-calibrated each cycle against realised outcomes, never fabricated constants. The score's job is triage, not automation: it ranks SKUs into candidate keep/expand/cut buckets that the decision rule then applies with the sample-sufficiency and confound gates. State plainly that a composite hides its inputs, so the three raw metrics travel with the score and any SKU near a boundary is inspected on its components, not its blended number.

included: the transparent weighted blend of sell-through, margin and inverse return rate
explicit owner-set, re-calibrated weights (not fabricated constants)
score-as-triage feeding the decision rule, raw metrics travel with it
excluded: the sample and confound gates (SAMPLE_SUFFICIENCY, ATTRIBUTION_CONFOUNDS)

pros.claim: A transparent weighted score ranks SKUs on all three metrics at once so a fast-but-unprofitable or profitable-but-returned SKU cannot hide
pros.example: a high-velocity SKU with heavy returns scores below a steady full-price one once the return penalty applies

cons.claim: Any weighting embeds a judgement, and a blended score can obscure which metric drove a verdict if the raw components are dropped
cons.example: two SKUs with the same composite can have opposite margin-vs-velocity profiles needing different actions

failure_modes: treating the composite as an automated verdict rather than triage, skipping the gates
hiding the raw metrics behind the blended score so boundary SKUs are mis-actioned
acceptance_tests: the transparent weighted blend, the explicit re-calibrated owner-set weights, and the score-as-triage (raw metrics travel with it) are stated
revisit_triggers: the business goal shifts (cash vs growth), changing the weights
realised outcomes show a weight mis-calibrated
a new metric is added to the blend

base.update_signal: the weights, goal, or a component metric changes the score

nodes.definition: The centrepiece decision rule [METHOD]: map each SKU's composite (with its raw components) to KEEP, EXPAND or CUT, but only after the sample-sufficiency gate and the confound/seasonality flags pass — an under-powered or confounded SKU is never force-decided, it goes to hold-and-tweak. The matrix: EXPAND a proven winner (strong sell-through AND positive contribution AND acceptable returns, sample-sufficient) by adding depth/variants; KEEP a solid steady performer (meets baseline on the blend) by reordering at its current breadth; CUT a structural loser (persistent low sell-through OR near/negative contribution after returns OR a quality/return failure, sample-sufficient) by discontinuing and liquidating. The rule is deliberately conservative on CUT inside the window and on EXPAND on a confounded number, because both errors are expensive: a wrong cut kills a good SKU, a wrong expand commits inventory cash to a false winner. All thresholds are owner-calibrated [METHOD]/[ESTIMATE] against the store baseline and reorder economics, not fabricated benchmarks.

included: the KEEP/EXPAND/CUT decision matrix gated on sufficiency and confounds
the conservative-on-cut-inside-window and conservative-on-confounded-expand stance
owner-calibrated thresholds against baseline and reorder economics

pros.claim: A gated three-way rule turns three metrics into a repeatable action while blocking noise-driven and promo-driven verdicts
pros.example: a strong-looking SKU that fails the confound flag is held, not expanded, avoiding cash committed to a false winner

cons.claim: A conservative rule slows decisions and can keep a mediocre SKU alive longer than a sharper heuristic would
cons.example: a SKU hovering at the KEEP/CUT boundary consumes shelf and attention across extra cycles

failure_modes: forcing a verdict on an under-powered or confounded SKU instead of routing it to hold
applying a fabricated benchmark threshold rather than the store-calibrated cut points
acceptance_tests: the KEEP/EXPAND/CUT matrix, its sufficiency+confound gates, the conservative stance on cut-in-window and confounded-expand, and owner-calibrated thresholds are all stated
revisit_triggers: the store baseline or reorder economics shift the calibrated thresholds
a wrong cut or wrong expand is discovered in review
the composite weights or gates change

base.update_signal: a threshold, gate, or a discovered wrong verdict changes the rule

nodes.definition: Execute the EXPAND branch: turn a proven winner into more revenue without over-committing. Expansion levers for plated jewelry, cheapest-risk first: reorder the exact SKU at greater depth; add close variants (new colour/finish — e.g. the rhodium-white and gold-tone of a hit shape, an alternate chain length, a stone-colour option); then extend the shape into an adjacent category (a hit stud into a matching huggie or pendant) to build a collection and cross-sell/stacking. Each expansion is itself a new hypothesis re-entered into the test protocol, and must clear the cannibalization check (adds incremental demand, not just steals the parent's sales) and the MOQ/cash gate (a plating run commits inventory). Expand on contribution-strong winners first, since expansion ties up more cash; a thin-margin winner is expanded cautiously. Never expand on a confounded or peak-season number.

included: depth reorder, colour/finish/length variants, adjacent-category extension
each expansion re-entered as a new test hypothesis
contribution-strong-first and confound/peak guardrails

pros.claim: Laddering expansion cheapest-risk-first (depth, then variant, then adjacent) grows a winner while keeping each step measurable
pros.example: reordering a hit stud at depth before committing a new pendant limits cash risk until the variant proves out

cons.claim: Expanding a winner multiplies SKUs and inventory cash and, unchecked, is the main engine of SKU bloat and cannibalization
cons.example: five colourways of one hit shape can split the same demand across five SKUs and five MOQs

failure_modes: expanding on a confounded or peak-season winner that will not hold
adding variants that cannibalize the parent without growing total demand
acceptance_tests: the depth/variant/adjacent expansion ladder, the re-enter-as-new-hypothesis rule, and the contribution-first + confound/peak + cannibalization/MOQ guardrails are stated
revisit_triggers: a winner's steady-state velocity is confirmed post-confound
a variant's cannibalization or margin comes in worse than the parent
MOQ/cash capacity for expansion changes

base.update_signal: a winner's confirmed velocity, a variant's result, or expansion capacity changes

nodes.definition: Execute the CUT branch: discontinue a sample-sufficient structural loser and recover the cash trapped in it. A loser is a SKU with persistent low sell-through, near/negative contribution after returns, or a quality/return failure — confirmed outside its window, past the sufficiency gate, and not explained by a fixable confound or listing issue. Cutting is not free: committed plating-run inventory must be cleared, so the CUT action includes a liquidation plan (markdown ladder, bundle with a winner, clearance) to convert dead stock to cash rather than leaving it on the shelf. The discipline is to cut decisively once the evidence is in — sunk plating cost is sunk and should not keep a loser alive (the sunk-cost trap) — while never cutting on noise. A cut SKU's learning (why it failed: shape, price, finish, category) is captured for FEEDBACK_TO_DEMAND, so the next candidate list is better.

included: discontinue a sufficiency-gated structural loser
a liquidation/markdown plan to recover trapped inventory cash
capturing the failure learning and avoiding the sunk-cost trap
excluded: routing the learning back to demand (FEEDBACK_TO_DEMAND)

pros.claim: Cutting decisively with a liquidation plan recovers cash and shelf from a confirmed loser instead of letting it bleed
pros.example: bundling a dead SKU with a winner clears its stock while lifting the winner's AOV

cons.claim: A cut is largely irreversible once inventory is liquidated and the listing removed, so a wrong cut permanently loses a SKU and its sunk plating cost
cons.example: liquidating a SKU that a later season would have sold forfeits both the stock and the re-listing option

failure_modes: keeping a confirmed loser alive to avoid writing off sunk plating cost (the sunk-cost trap)
cutting on noise or a fixable confound before the evidence is in
acceptance_tests: the sufficiency-gated cut, the liquidation/markdown plan to recover cash, and the sunk-cost-trap warning with failure-learning capture are stated
revisit_triggers: a loser's failure reason turns out to be a fixable listing/confound issue
liquidation is slower than planned, stranding cash
a seasonal window would have changed the verdict

base.update_signal: a loser's reason, liquidation pace, or a seasonal reconsideration changes the cut

nodes.definition: Handle the ambiguous middle the binary keep/cut misses: a SKU that is under-powered (failed the sample gate), confounded (its number was driven by exposure/price/season), or simply middling (near the keep/cut boundary) is HELD and TWEAKED, not force-decided. Tweak levers before any cut: fix the listing (better photography, clearer sizing chart, improved copy), normalise exposure (give a buried SKU a fair impression share, or remove an artificial boost), or adjust price into the tested band — then re-measure over a fresh window. Hold-and-tweak is the protocol's way of not throwing away a possibly-good SKU on a fixable problem, and it is bounded: a SKU that stays ambiguous after one or two tweak cycles is escalated to a cut, so hold does not become a graveyard of undecided SKUs consuming cash and attention indefinitely.

included: hold-and-tweak for under-powered/confounded/middling SKUs
listing/exposure/price tweak levers then re-measure
a bounded number of tweak cycles before escalation to cut

pros.claim: A bounded hold-and-tweak path rescues fixable SKUs (bad photo, unfair exposure, wrong price) that a binary cut would waste
pros.example: a middling SKU jumps to a keep after a photography and sizing-chart fix, no product change needed

cons.claim: Hold-and-tweak can become an indefinite limbo that ties up cash and attention if the cycle bound is not enforced
cons.example: a SKU tweaked five times without resolution is really a slow, expensive cut

failure_modes: letting a SKU sit in hold indefinitely without escalating to a cut
tweaking product/price without re-measuring over a fresh window before re-deciding
acceptance_tests: the hold-and-tweak levers (listing/exposure/price + re-measure) and the bounded-cycles-before-escalation rule are stated
revisit_triggers: a held SKU exhausts its tweak-cycle budget
a listing/exposure/price tweak changes its metrics
the sample or confound status of a held SKU resolves

base.update_signal: a held SKU's tweak result, cycle budget, or status changes

nodes.definition: Carry the hard constraint that plating-batch MOQ and working capital impose on how fast a SKU can be cut or expanded, inherited from the supply-side and economics specialists. Expansion is not free: a variant or reorder commits a minimum plating-run quantity of inventory cash before a single unit sells, so a winner can only be expanded as fast as the cash cycle funds — a profitable-per-unit expansion can still strain cash. A cut is not clean either: the SKU carries committed stock (already-plated inventory and possibly a minimum reorder already placed) that must be liquidated, so the true cost of a cut includes clearing dead inventory. This constraint sets the floor speed of iteration: the refresh cadence and the keep/cut/expand tempo cannot out-run the MOQ reorder cycle or the working-capital available to fund newness. Actual MOQ and cash figures are [UNKNOWN] here; the constraint is [FACT-structural], the magnitudes inherited.

included: plating-MOQ and working-capital as the floor on cut/expand speed
expansion commits inventory cash before sale; cut must liquidate committed stock
iteration tempo bounded by the reorder cycle and available cash
excluded: deriving the MOQ or cash magnitudes (supply/economics specialists)

pros.claim: Naming the MOQ/cash floor stops the protocol from prescribing an iteration tempo the cash cycle cannot fund
pros.example: a plan to expand three winners at once is checked against whether three plating runs can be funded before their stock sells

cons.claim: The constraint is structural but its magnitude is [UNKNOWN] here, so it flags a limit without sizing it until the economics inputs land
cons.example: whether a given expansion strains cash depends on the actual MOQ and payback the economics specialist owns

failure_modes: prescribing a refresh/expand tempo that out-runs the MOQ reorder cycle and available cash
treating a cut as costless while committed plating inventory sits unsold
acceptance_tests: the plating-MOQ/working-capital floor on cut and expand speed, the commit-cash-before-sale reality, and the iteration-tempo bound are stated as a [FACT-structural] constraint with magnitudes inherited
revisit_triggers: the economics specialist updates MOQ or working-capital figures
a supplier changes plating-run minimums or lead time
available launch/expansion cash changes

base.update_signal: an MOQ, lead-time or working-capital figure changes the constraint

nodes.definition: Test whether a new or expanded SKU adds incremental demand or merely redistributes existing demand [METHOD], because winner-expansion is the main way a catalog bloats without growing revenue. When a variant launches (a new colourway of a hit shape, an adjacent-category extension), compare total category/collection velocity before and after against the new SKU's own sales: if the new SKU sells 20 units/week but the parent and siblings drop by ~18, it cannibalized rather than grew the business, adding a SKU, an MOQ and photography cost for almost no incremental revenue. The check gates expansion: a variant that mostly cannibalizes is not a true expansion win and should be consolidated back, while one that grows total demand justifies its SKU. Perfect attribution is impossible (buyers substitute), so this is an [ESTIMATE] read of incrementality, not an exact split — but even a rough before/after comparison catches the worst cannibalizers.

included: before/after total-velocity vs new-SKU-sales incrementality read
gate expansion on incremental (not cannibalized) demand
incrementality as an [ESTIMATE], not an exact split

pros.claim: A before/after incrementality check catches variants that split existing demand instead of growing it, the worst driver of silent bloat
pros.example: a fourth colourway that lifts its own sales but drops the other three by the same amount is flagged as cannibalizing, not expanding

cons.claim: Incrementality cannot be measured exactly because buyers substitute, so the check is a directional [ESTIMATE] that can misread a small effect
cons.example: a modest true lift can be masked by a concurrent traffic change

failure_modes: counting a cannibalizing variant's own sales as growth while ignoring the parent's decline
adding endless colourways that split one demand pool across many SKUs and MOQs
acceptance_tests: the before/after total-velocity vs new-SKU-sales incrementality read, the gate-expansion-on-incremental rule, and the [ESTIMATE] caveat are stated
revisit_triggers: a new variant's parent/sibling sales drop after its launch
total category velocity is flat despite added SKUs
a traffic change confounds the before/after read

base.update_signal: a variant launch, a sibling-sales drop, or a traffic change alters incrementality

nodes.definition: Design the refresh cadence: the rhythm of introducing new candidate SKUs and dropping discontinued ones [METHOD], set so the catalog stays fresh (a young-women fashion audience rewards newness) without out-running either the measurement window or the MOQ/cash cycle. Two governors. (1) Do not launch new SKUs faster than you can measure them — if the window is ~4-8 weeks, a rolling drop of a small batch each window keeps every SKU testable, whereas dumping many at once means none gets a fair, confound-free read. (2) Do not commit newness the cash cycle cannot fund — the MOQ constraint bounds how many plating runs of new candidates can be in flight. A workable pattern is a small rolling refresh synced to the window and reorder cycle (drop a few, cut a few), not a big seasonal reset. The specific tempo is an [ESTIMATE] tuned to traffic and cash; the principle (cadence bounded by window and MOQ) is the fixed [METHOD].

included: rolling small-batch refresh synced to window and MOQ cycle
the two governors (measurability and cash)
tempo as [ESTIMATE], cadence-bound-by-window-and-MOQ as [METHOD]
excluded: the bloat-control discipline the cadence serves (SKU_BLOAT_AVOIDANCE)

pros.claim: A rolling refresh synced to the window keeps every new SKU measurable and the catalog fresh without a chaotic big reset
pros.example: dropping two candidates and cutting two losers each window keeps the count stable and every launch testable

cons.claim: Too slow a cadence lets the assortment go stale for a newness-hungry audience; too fast breaks measurability and cash — the tuning is delicate
cons.example: a quarterly-only refresh may bore repeat visitors while a weekly one out-runs the test window

failure_modes: launching more new SKUs per window than can be measured confound-free
committing more new plating runs than the cash cycle can fund
acceptance_tests: the rolling refresh synced to the window and MOQ cycle, the measurability and cash governors, and the [ESTIMATE]-tempo/[METHOD]-principle split are stated
revisit_triggers: the measurement window or MOQ cycle changes, moving the cadence bound
the audience shows newness fatigue or staleness
cash capacity for new launches changes

base.update_signal: the window, MOQ cycle, audience-newness signal, or cash capacity changes the cadence

nodes.definition: Enforce the discipline that keeps the catalog from bloating into a low-velocity long tail [METHOD]. Every SKU carries cost beyond its COGS: inventory cash, a plating-run MOQ, photography and listing effort, and buyer cognitive load (too many near-identical options depress conversion). Left unchecked, winner-expansion and refresh both grow the count faster than demand. The controls: a soft cap on active SKU count for a small operation; a one-in-one-out rule (a new SKU should displace the weakest active one unless it clears a higher bar); a hard cut rule for persistent losers so the tail is pruned every cycle; and the cannibalization check so variants must add demand. The goal is a tight, high-velocity assortment where most SKUs earn their shelf, not a sprawling catalog where a few winners subsidise a long dead tail. This is the direct answer to the owner's 'avoid SKU bloat' concern and the counterweight to expansion.

included: the full SKU carrying cost (cash, MOQ, photography, cognitive load)
soft cap + one-in-one-out + hard cut + cannibalization controls
tight high-velocity assortment as the goal

pros.claim: One-in-one-out plus a hard cut rule keeps the assortment tight and high-velocity, so most SKUs earn their shelf
pros.example: a soft cap forcing a new SKU to displace the weakest active one prevents the catalog creeping from 6 to 60 low-velocity pieces

cons.claim: Over-tight caps can prune a slow-burn SKU that would have matured or a strategic breadth piece that anchors a collection
cons.example: a one-in-one-out rule might cut a niche piece that lifts the brand's perceived range

failure_modes: letting winner-expansion and refresh grow the count faster than demand, building a dead long tail
cutting a strategic breadth/anchor SKU purely on velocity
acceptance_tests: the SKU carrying-cost list, the soft-cap + one-in-one-out + hard-cut + cannibalization controls, and the tight-assortment goal are stated
revisit_triggers: active SKU count creeps past the soft cap
conversion drops as near-identical options proliferate
a pruned SKU is later shown to have been maturing or strategic

base.update_signal: the SKU count, conversion, or a pruned-SKU reconsideration changes the discipline

nodes.definition: Close the loop by routing each cycle's learnings back to the demand-side specialists [METHOD], so the test-and-iterate protocol improves the next candidate list rather than only pruning the current one. What flows back: which shapes/finishes/categories won or lost and why (to kb1_signal_synthesis_ranking and the S1 market read); which return reasons recurred (to the form specialist's sizing/fit work and the materials specialist's plating-quality work); and where the pre-launch poll or signal was wrong (to the poll specialist, correcting for the self-selection bias kb1 already flagged — realised sell-through is a truer signal than a poll vote). This makes the six-SKU launch the first turn of a learning system: real purchase data (the strongest signal) re-weights the priors that pick the next launch set, so each cycle's candidate list is better-grounded than the last. All fed-back reads carry their [ESTIMATE]/[METHOD]/[UNKNOWN] tags; realised store data is the one genuinely measured input.

included: routing win/loss, return-reason and poll-error learnings back to kb1/S1/poll/form/materials
realised purchase data re-weighting the next-cycle priors
carrying tags on fed-back reads
excluded: the poll instrument and market-read work themselves (poll and market specialists)

pros.claim: Feeding realised purchase data back makes the strongest possible signal re-weight the priors, so each launch set is better-grounded than the last
pros.example: a shape that beat its poll rank corrects the poll's self-selection bias for the next candidate ranking

cons.claim: Over-fitting the next launch to one cycle's winners can narrow the assortment and miss untested demand
cons.example: chasing only the last cycle's hit finish may starve exploration of a new category

failure_modes: treating the launch as a one-off decision and not feeding learnings back
over-fitting the next candidate list to a single cycle's noisy winners
acceptance_tests: the win/loss + return-reason + poll-error feedback routes to kb1/S1/poll/form/materials and the realised-data-re-weights-priors loop are stated with tags carried
revisit_triggers: a cycle's realised data contradicts a pre-launch signal
a recurring return reason implicates a form or materials fix
the next candidate list is being assembled

base.update_signal: a cycle's realised data, a return-reason pattern, or a new candidate list changes the feedback

nodes.definition: Enforce the binding honesty discipline across the protocol so its structure is trusted while its numbers are not over-read. Solid [FACT] (definitions and mechanisms, load-bearing): the metric definitions (sell-through, return rate, contribution margin); the statistical-power basis of the window and sufficiency gates; the jewelry gift-cycle seasonality; the plated-jewelry return drivers (sizing, plating wear/tarnish, nickel EN1811 0.5 ug/cm2/week); the MOQ/working-capital constraint as structural. Explicit [METHOD] (how to measure/decide, not a fabricated answer): every threshold — 'good' sell-through, acceptable return, minimum margin, the composite weights, the keep/cut/expand cut points, the SKU cap, the refresh tempo — all owner-calibrated against the store's own baseline and economics. Genuinely [UNKNOWN] until measured: this store's realised per-SKU sell-through, return and margin rates. The rule: never assert a benchmark number as a measured market fact; the protocol supplies the method and the store's own data supplies the numbers.

included: the [FACT] definitions/mechanisms vs the [METHOD] thresholds vs the [UNKNOWN] realised rates
the never-assert-a-benchmark-as-fact rule
method-from-protocol, numbers-from-store-data
excluded: the substantive metric and rule content (the other nodes)
the demand-side poll/market honesty discipline (those specialists)

pros.claim: A single ledger separating fact definitions from calibrated-method thresholds and unknown realised rates keeps the protocol trustworthy without inventing benchmarks
pros.example: tagging the sell-through formula [FACT] but every threshold [METHOD] tells a reader exactly what is measured vs owner-set

cons.claim: Heavy tagging frustrates a user who wants a single 'good sell-through is X%' answer the evidence cannot honestly give
cons.example: the owner asking for a target number must accept a method to derive it from their own data instead

failure_modes: asserting a fabricated benchmark (e.g. 'average return rate is X%') as a measured fact
hardening an owner-calibrated threshold into a claimed industry standard
acceptance_tests: the [FACT] definitions/mechanisms, the [METHOD] owner-calibrated thresholds, the [UNKNOWN] realised rates, and the never-assert-a-benchmark rule are all enumerated
revisit_triggers: a [METHOD] threshold is calibrated from accumulated store data
an [UNKNOWN] realised rate becomes measured
a [FACT] definition or mechanism is revised

base.update_signal: a threshold is calibrated, a realised rate is measured, or a fact is revised

nodes.definition: Compose the protocol's output: for each launched SKU, the verdict (KEEP / EXPAND / CUT / HOLD-and-tweak) with the metrics and gates that justified it; the refresh calendar (what drops in and out next window, synced to the measurement window and MOQ cycle); and the standing guardrails (never decide inside the window or on a confounded/peak number; sample-sufficiency gate; one-in-one-out and hard-cut bloat discipline; cannibalization and MOQ checks on expansion). Deliver this as a repeatable cycle the owner runs each window, not a one-off. State the clean boundary: this protocol owns the post-launch test-and-iterate loop and its verdicts; it does NOT own the initial 6-SKU construction (kb2), the pre-launch signal synthesis (kb1), or the COGS/price/CAC model (economics) — it consumes their outputs and feeds learnings back. The whole handoff carries the honesty ledger's tags: the decisions are method-grounded, the store's own realised data supplies every number.

included: per-SKU verdict + justification, the refresh calendar, and the standing guardrails
the protocol as a repeatable per-window cycle
the clean boundary vs kb1/kb2/economics with feedback back to them
excluded: the demand synthesis (kb1) and the COGS/price model (economics)

pros.claim: A composed per-cycle handoff turns the protocol into a repeatable operating rhythm the owner can run without re-deriving it each window
pros.example: each window closes with a verdict sheet, a refresh calendar and the guardrails, ready to run again

cons.claim: A repeatable cycle can ossify into ritual if the guardrails and thresholds are not re-calibrated as the store's data accumulates
cons.example: running the same cut points for a year despite a changed baseline mis-judges SKUs

failure_modes: delivering a one-off verdict set instead of a repeatable per-window cycle
letting the handoff drift into owning the launch-set construction or the economics model it should only consume
acceptance_tests: the per-SKU verdict+justification, the refresh calendar, the standing guardrails, the repeatable-cycle framing, and the clean boundary vs kb1/kb2/economics with feedback are all stated
revisit_triggers: a window closes and the cycle is re-run
a guardrail or threshold needs re-calibration from accumulated data
an upstream input (launch set, signal, economics) changes

conflict_axes.name: decision_speed_vs_signal_confidence
conflict_axes.description: Cutting or expanding fast frees cash and speeds iteration, but a verdict inside the window or on a thin sample is noise; confidence and speed trade off directly.
poles: wait for an in-window, sample-sufficient signal
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: gate every cut/expand on the window and sufficiency; route under-powered SKUs to hold-and-tweak rather than force a fast but noisy verdict

conflict_axes.name: velocity_vs_profitability
conflict_axes.description: A fast-selling SKU is not necessarily a keeper if its contribution is thin or its returns are heavy; sell-through and margin can point opposite ways.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use the composite score net of returns and markdowns so velocity and profitability are weighed together, and never keep a high-velocity, near-zero-contribution SKU

conflict_axes.name: raw_signal_vs_confound_adjusted
conflict_axes.description: A raw sell-through number is easy to act on but may be driven by ad spend, price, a feature or a seasonal peak rather than intrinsic product appeal.
poles: act on the raw measured number
act only on the confound/season-adjusted read
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: flag exposure/price/season per SKU before any verdict; where a confound dominates, hold and re-measure at normalised exposure rather than expanding on the inflated number

conflict_axes.name: expand_winners_vs_avoid_bloat
conflict_axes.description: Expanding proven winners with variants grows revenue but multiplies SKUs, inventory and cannibalization risk, working against a tight assortment.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: gate expansion on the cannibalization check and one-in-one-out; a variant must add incremental demand and displace a weaker SKU, not just grow the count

conflict_axes.name: cut_decisively_vs_sunk_cost
conflict_axes.description: A confirmed loser should be cut to recover shelf and cash, but committed plating inventory and the temptation to recoup sunk cost push toward keeping it alive.
poles: keep it to work off sunk inventory
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: cut on the evidence and liquidate committed stock via markdown/bundle; treat sunk plating cost as sunk and do not let it keep a confirmed loser in the assortment

conflict_axes.name: freshness_vs_measurability
conflict_axes.description: A fast refresh keeps the catalog fresh for a newness-hungry audience but launching many SKUs at once denies each a fair, confound-free measurement window.
poles: refresh slow enough to measure each SKU
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: run a small rolling refresh synced to the measurement window and MOQ cycle so every new SKU still gets a clean test

conflict_axes.name: iteration_tempo_vs_cash_cycle
conflict_axes.description: Rapid cut/expand/refresh iteration is desirable but each expansion or new candidate commits plating-MOQ inventory cash that the working-capital cycle must fund first.
poles: iterate as fast as the data allows
bound tempo to the MOQ/cash cycle
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: cap in-flight new/expanded plating runs to what the cash cycle funds; the iteration tempo cannot out-run the MOQ reorder and working-capital reality

conflict_axes.name: prior_expectation_vs_realised_data
conflict_axes.description: The pre-launch ranking (poll + market read) is a prior; realised purchase data is a stronger but later signal, and they can disagree about a SKU.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: let realised sell-through override the prior once sample-sufficient, and feed the disagreement back to correct the poll's self-selection bias for the next cycle

conflict_axes.name: single_composite_verdict_vs_raw_components
conflict_axes.description: A blended composite score is convenient for ranking but can hide which metric drove a verdict, mis-actioning a boundary SKU.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use the composite for triage only and inspect any boundary SKU on its raw sell-through, margin and return components before a keep/cut/expand action

edge_cases.description: A SKU is cut after a slow first week, inside its measurement window, on a handful of orders
edge_cases.trigger: a keep/cut verdict is issued before the window closes and before the sample-sufficiency gate passes
edge_cases.mitigation: block any verdict until both the window and the per-SKU minimum-sales gate pass; route the SKU to hold-and-tweak meanwhile

edge_cases.description: A SKU is expanded because a one-off paid-ad boost or homepage feature made it look like a winner
edge_cases.trigger: an expand verdict is issued on a confounded sell-through number without normalising exposure
edge_cases.mitigation: flag the SKU's ad/feature/price history; hold and re-measure at normal exposure before committing an expansion plating run

edge_cases.description: A SKU launched only in the Q4 or Valentine's peak is expanded on its peak-season number and underperforms at steady state
edge_cases.trigger: an expand decision uses a peak-window sell-through as if it were the steady-state rate
edge_cases.mitigation: normalise the peak-window read against the store's traffic index or span a non-peak window before expanding

edge_cases.description: A high-velocity SKU is kept while a 30% return rate and a 20% markdown quietly drive its contribution near zero
edge_cases.trigger: a keep verdict rests on sell-through alone, ignoring the return- and markdown-netted contribution
edge_cases.mitigation: read contribution net of returns and markdowns in the composite; a fast SKU near zero contribution is a cut/fix candidate, not a keep

edge_cases.description: A confirmed structural loser is kept alive to avoid writing off its already-plated inventory (sunk-cost trap)
edge_cases.trigger: a cut is deferred because committed plating stock has not sold through
edge_cases.mitigation: cut on the evidence and liquidate the committed stock via markdown/bundle; treat sunk plating cost as sunk

edge_cases.description: Winner-expansion adds a fourth colourway that lifts its own sales but drops the other three by nearly the same amount
edge_cases.trigger: a variant is counted as growth without a before/after cannibalization check
edge_cases.mitigation: compare total category velocity before/after against the variant's own sales; consolidate a cannibalizing variant back

edge_cases.description: The catalog creeps from 6 to dozens of low-velocity SKUs as expansion and refresh outpace demand
edge_cases.trigger: no soft cap or one-in-one-out rule bounds SKU growth across cycles
edge_cases.mitigation: enforce a soft SKU cap, one-in-one-out, and a hard cut of persistent losers each cycle

edge_cases.description: Many new SKUs are dropped at once, so none gets a fair, confound-free measurement window
edge_cases.trigger: the refresh cadence launches a large batch simultaneously rather than a small rolling set
edge_cases.mitigation: shift to a small rolling refresh synced to the window so each new SKU is measurable in isolation

edge_cases.description: An owner asks for the 'good' sell-through or return benchmark and a fabricated industry number is supplied as fact
edge_cases.trigger: a threshold is asserted as a measured market statistic rather than a store-calibrated method
edge_cases.mitigation: supply the method to derive the threshold from the store's own baseline and economics; tag it [METHOD], never a benchmark fact

edge_cases.description: A low-traffic SKU never accumulates enough sales to reach sufficiency and sits in hold indefinitely
edge_cases.trigger: the sufficiency gate is never met because the SKU gets almost no impressions
edge_cases.mitigation: give the SKU a fair exposure share as a tweak; if still under-powered after a bounded number of cycles, escalate to a cut on a traffic-side decision

edge_cases.description: An expansion is committed that the working-capital cycle cannot fund before the new stock sells
edge_cases.trigger: multiple plating runs are ordered at once beyond available cash
edge_cases.mitigation: cap in-flight new/expanded plating runs to what the cash cycle funds; sequence expansions rather than committing them together

edge_cases.description: The same cut points and composite weights are run unchanged for a year despite a shifted store baseline
edge_cases.trigger: thresholds are treated as fixed rather than re-calibrated from accumulated data each cycle
edge_cases.mitigation: re-calibrate the weights and cut points against the store's updated baseline each cycle as part of the handoff

workflow.action: Accept the launch set and baseline as test input
workflow.description: Record per-SKU units/price/category/launch-date and the kb1 prior expectation, and frame launch as the start of a measured test against the store baseline
workflow.gate: the 6 SKUs, their inputs and the store baseline are stated as accepted test input with the per-SKU prior

workflow.description: State sell-through, return/quality and contribution-margin definitions [FACT] and the fact-vs-calibrated-threshold split
workflow.gate: the three metric definitions and the fact/threshold split are stated

workflow.action: Fix the measurement window and sample gate
workflow.description: Set the time-and-volume window on its statistical+seasonal basis and the per-SKU sufficiency gate; do not judge before both pass
workflow.gate: the window [METHOD] and the sample-sufficiency gate are stated with their bases

workflow.description: Compute units-sold/units-received and velocity against the store baseline, with winner/loser bands flagged as calibrated method
workflow.gate: per-SKU sell-through and velocity are stated against baseline with bands flagged [METHOD]

workflow.description: Compute returns/units-sold with plated-jewelry reason codes (sizing, plating wear/tarnish, nickel reaction)
workflow.gate: per-SKU return/complaint rate with reason codes is stated, realised rates flagged [UNKNOWN]

workflow.action: Bring in contribution margin net of returns
workflow.description: Consume per-SKU contribution net of returns/markdowns from economics; flag negative-contribution-despite-velocity as a cut signal
workflow.gate: contribution net of returns/markdowns is stated as an inherited input with the cut signal noted

workflow.description: Record each SKU's ad/price/feature/season history and normalise or hold confounded SKUs before any verdict
workflow.gate: the confounds and the seasonal adjustment are flagged per SKU before verdict

workflow.action: Blend metrics into a composite score
workflow.description: Compute the transparent weighted blend with explicit owner-set weights; carry the raw components with it as triage
workflow.gate: the weighted composite with explicit weights and travelling raw components is stated

workflow.description: Map each sample-sufficient, confound-cleared SKU to KEEP/EXPAND/CUT; route the rest to hold-and-tweak
workflow.gate: each SKU has a gated KEEP/EXPAND/CUT/HOLD verdict with its justification

workflow.action: Execute expand, cut and hold with bloat and MOQ checks
workflow.description: Expand winners (cannibalization + MOQ checked), liquidate losers, hold-and-tweak the middle, all under one-in-one-out discipline
workflow.gate: expand/cut/hold actions are stated with cannibalization, MOQ and bloat guardrails

workflow.action: Set the refresh cadence and avoid bloat
workflow.description: Define a rolling refresh synced to the window and MOQ cycle with one-in-one-out and a soft SKU cap
workflow.gate: the rolling refresh cadence and bloat discipline are stated within the window/MOQ bounds

workflow.action: Compose the honest handoff and feedback loop
workflow.description: Deliver the verdict set, refresh calendar and guardrails as a repeatable per-window cycle, feed learnings back, and carry the honesty tags
workflow.gate: the verdicts, refresh calendar, guardrails, repeatable-cycle framing and feedback+honesty tags are stated

dominance_rules.rule: The window and sample-sufficiency gates dominate any early keep/cut verdict
dominance_rules.rationale: a verdict inside the window or on a thin sample is noise, and cutting a good SKU early is the most common and costly test-and-iterate error
dominance_rules.trigger: a cut/expand verdict is proposed before the window closes or the sufficiency gate passes
dominance_rules.action: block the verdict and route the SKU to hold-and-tweak until both gates pass

dominance_rules.rule: Contribution net of returns dominates raw velocity in the keep decision
dominance_rules.rationale: a fast SKU at near-zero contribution after returns and markdowns loses money faster the more it sells
dominance_rules.trigger: a keep/expand verdict rests on sell-through while contribution net of returns is near or below zero
dominance_rules.action: treat the SKU as a cut/fix candidate despite its velocity

dominance_rules.rule: Confound- and season-adjusted reads dominate the raw number for expansion
dominance_rules.rationale: expanding on a promo- or peak-driven false winner commits inventory cash to demand that will not hold
dominance_rules.trigger: an expand verdict uses a raw sell-through inflated by ad spend, a feature or a seasonal peak
dominance_rules.action: normalise exposure/season and re-measure before committing an expansion plating run

dominance_rules.rule: The cannibalization check dominates raw variant sales in judging an expansion
dominance_rules.rationale: a variant that only redistributes existing demand adds SKUs and cost without growing revenue
dominance_rules.trigger: an expansion is judged on the new SKU's own sales without a before/after total-velocity comparison
dominance_rules.action: credit only incremental demand; consolidate a cannibalizing variant back

dominance_rules.rule: The evidence-based cut dominates the sunk-cost of committed inventory
dominance_rules.rationale: sunk plating cost is sunk; keeping a confirmed loser alive to recoup it wastes shelf and cash
dominance_rules.trigger: a cut is deferred because already-plated stock has not sold
dominance_rules.action: cut on the evidence and liquidate the committed stock via markdown or bundle

dominance_rules.rule: SKU-bloat discipline dominates unconstrained winner-expansion and refresh
dominance_rules.rationale: expansion and newness both grow the count faster than demand, building a costly dead long tail
dominance_rules.trigger: active SKU count grows without a cap, one-in-one-out, or a hard cut of losers
dominance_rules.action: enforce the soft cap, one-in-one-out, and a hard cut each cycle

dominance_rules.rule: The MOQ/cash cycle dominates the desired iteration tempo
dominance_rules.rationale: each expansion or new candidate commits plating-MOQ inventory cash the working-capital cycle must fund first
dominance_rules.trigger: a refresh/expand plan commits more plating runs than the cash cycle can fund
dominance_rules.action: cap in-flight runs to available cash and sequence rather than commit together

dominance_rules.rule: Realised purchase data dominates the pre-launch prior once sample-sufficient
dominance_rules.rationale: measured sell-through is a stronger signal than a poll vote subject to self-selection bias
dominance_rules.trigger: realised, sample-sufficient data disagrees with the pre-launch ranking for a SKU
dominance_rules.action: defer to the realised data and feed the disagreement back to correct the poll/market prior

dominance_rules.rule: A benchmark stated as a measured fact is dominated by the store-calibrated method
dominance_rules.rationale: no honest industry sell-through/return/margin benchmark exists for this store; only its own data supplies the numbers
dominance_rules.trigger: a threshold is asserted as a measured market statistic
dominance_rules.action: replace it with the [METHOD] to derive the threshold from the store's own baseline and economics

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix the measurement window and sample gate before launch, not after the first slow week
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a premature cut of a good SKU that has to be re-listed and re-tested, or a defence of an early verdict that was noise

anti_rework_rules.rule: Record each SKU's ad/price/feature/season history from launch, in the same step as the sell-through read
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering after an expansion that the winner was promotion-driven and having to unwind committed inventory

anti_rework_rules.rule: Read contribution net of returns and markdowns from the first metric pass
anti_rework_rules.prevents: keeping a high-velocity, high-return SKU whose true contribution only surfaces later, forcing a delayed cut

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the cannibalization before/after check before crediting an expansion as growth
anti_rework_rules.prevents: stacking colourways that split one demand pool and having to consolidate the bloated variants later

anti_rework_rules.rule: Sync the refresh cadence to the measurement window and MOQ cycle from the outset
anti_rework_rules.prevents: launching more SKUs than can be measured or funded, then re-sequencing the whole refresh after cash or measurability breaks

anti_rework_rules.rule: Set a soft SKU cap and one-in-one-out rule before expansion begins
anti_rework_rules.prevents: the catalog bloating into a dead long tail that later needs a painful mass cull

anti_rework_rules.rule: Tag every threshold as owner-calibrated [METHOD] when first stated, never as a benchmark fact
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a fabricated benchmark circulating as measured truth and having to be retracted and re-derived from store data

anti_rework_rules.rule: Pair every cut with a liquidation plan when the cut is decided
anti_rework_rules.prevents: committed plating inventory stranding cash on the shelf after a SKU is discontinued

iteration_protocol.trigger: a SKU's measurement window closes and it passes the sample-sufficiency gate
iteration_protocol.action: run the composite score, apply the keep/cut/expand rule, and record the verdict with its justification

iteration_protocol.trigger: a confound (ad burst, price change, feature, seasonal peak) is found to have driven a SKU's read
iteration_protocol.action: hold the SKU, normalise exposure/season, and re-measure over a fresh window before any verdict

iteration_protocol.trigger: a return-reason spike or a plating-quality/nickel/sizing complaint appears on a SKU
iteration_protocol.action: re-read the return rate, route the fix to the form/materials specialists, and re-judge the SKU's contribution

iteration_protocol.trigger: an expanded variant's parent/sibling sales drop after its launch
iteration_protocol.action: run the cannibalization check and consolidate the variant back if it only redistributed demand

iteration_protocol.trigger: the economics specialist updates COGS/price or the supplier changes plating-run MOQ or lead time
iteration_protocol.action: re-compute contribution, re-scope the MOQ/cash constraint, and re-bound the refresh cadence and expansion tempo

iteration_protocol.trigger: active SKU count creeps past the soft cap or conversion drops as near-identical options proliferate
iteration_protocol.action: enforce one-in-one-out and hard-cut the weakest persistent losers to restore a tight assortment

iteration_protocol.trigger: a full cycle closes and the next launch set is being assembled
iteration_protocol.action: feed realised win/loss and return-reason learnings back to re-weight the priors and re-calibrate the composite weights and cut points

priority_rationale: The launch-baseline input and metric definitions come first because every verdict depends on an agreed test frame and agreed metric formulas; the measurement window and sample-sufficiency gates follow because they decide when a metric may be read at all; the three per-metric measurements and the confound/seasonality adjustments come next because they produce the clean per-SKU signal; the composite score and the keep/cut/expand rule then convert that signal into gated verdicts; the expand/cut/hold executions, the MOQ constraint, the cannibalization check, the refresh cadence and the bloat discipline apply and bound those verdicts in the real cash and assortment; and the feedback loop, honesty ledger and iteration handoff come last because they close the learning loop, tag every number, and compose the repeatable per-window cycle.
